story: Geomorphic AI forms Golden Dyke Exploration LLC in Alaska as two USGS Earth MRI funded DGGS airborne surveys over the Kuskokwim region go public

claims.claim: Geomorphic AI announced two wholly owned subsidiaries, Masi Resources S.A.C. in Peru and Golden Dyke Exploration LLC in Alaska.
claims.verbatim: two wholly owned subsidiaries: Masi Resources S.A.C. in Peru and Golden Dyke Exploration LLC in Alaska.
claims.source_outlet: Geomorphic AI (company news release via Newsfile)
claims.notes: Company's own release. Corroborated by North of 60 Mining News (Shane Lasley), which calls Golden Dyke 'Geomorphic AI's wholly owned Alaska subsidiary'.

claims.claim: Geomorphic AI dated its Alaska and Peru subsidiary announcement October 20th from Portland, Oregon.
claims.verbatim: Portland, Oregon--(Newsfile Corp. - October 20, 2026)
claims.source_outlet: Geomorphic AI (company news release via Newsfile)
claims.notes: Inside the October 11th to 21st window. The verbatim dateline contains dashes from the source; do not reproduce them in slide copy.

claims.claim: Geomorphic AI describes itself as an AI-driven minerals prospect generator.
claims.verbatim: an AI-driven minerals prospect generator,
claims.source_outlet: Geomorphic AI (company news release via Newsfile)
claims.notes: Self-description. Boilerplate adds 'Using systematic, data-driven screening of geological databases and historic datasets, the Company identifies overlooked mineral systems in prospective jurisdictions'.

claims.claim: Geomorphic AI says it advances projects through joint ventures, earn-in agreements and other partnerships while retaining a continuing interest.
claims.verbatim: advances these projects through joint ventures, earn-in agreements and other partnerships
claims.source_outlet: Geomorphic AI (company news release via Newsfile)
claims.notes: Boilerplate continues 'while Geomorphic retains a continuing interest'. North of 60 Mining News independently reports projects 'would then be advanced through joint ventures, earn-in agreements, and other partnerships'.

claims.claim: Geomorphic AI says its role is to generate and package targets and not to fund or operate drilling itself.
claims.value: not to fund or operate drilling
claims.verbatim: The Company's role is to generate and package quality targets - not to fund or operate drilling itself.
claims.source_outlet: Geomorphic AI (company news release via Newsfile)
claims.notes: Company boilerplate. The verbatim contains a hyphen used as a dash in the source; paraphrase in slide copy.

claims.claim: Geomorphic AI has not named any Alaska properties and says it expects to announce its first projects soon.
claims.verbatim: we are excited to be announcing our first projects soon.
claims.source_outlet: Geomorphic AI (company news release via Newsfile)
claims.notes: Forward-looking company statement; phrase as 'says it expects to'. North of 60 Mining News confirms 'Geomorphic AI has not yet identified specific properties acquired through Golden Dyke Exploration'.

claims.claim: Geomorphic AI Chief Executive Officer Mark Sumner said "Peru and Alaska are two of the most prospective places in the world to explore for copper and gold, and we now have our own company in each."
claims.verbatim: Peru and Alaska are two of the most prospective places in the world to explore for copper and gold, and we now have our own company in each.
claims.source_outlet: Geomorphic AI (company news release via Newsfile)
claims.notes: Attribution on page reads 'Geomorphic AI Chief Executive Officer, Mark Sumner,'. Promotional opinion, attribute it as his. First clause also quoted by North of 60 Mining News.

claims.claim: Geomorphic AI's release says decades of USGS and State geochemistry and mapping in Alaska are being extended by new State airborne geophysical surveys.
claims.verbatim: decades of USGS and State geochemistry and mapping are being extended by new State airborne geophysical surveys.
claims.source_outlet: Geomorphic AI (company news release via Newsfile)
claims.notes: The release does NOT name DGGS, Earth MRI or any specific survey. Do not write that Golden Dyke uses the Ganes Creek or Aniak data; see C10.

claims.claim: Geomorphic AI was founded early in 2026, according to North of 60 Mining News.
claims.verbatim: Founded early in 2026 by a team with experience on both the mining and technology sides of the equation,
claims.source_outlet: North of 60 Mining News
claims.notes: Single secondary source; the company release and homepage fetched give no founding year. Attribute to North of 60 Mining News. Page dated October 21st although the URL path reads 2026/10/23 (print issue date).

claims.claim: Geomorphic AI has not announced whether it has used Earth MRI datasets in its Alaska targeting work, according to North of 60 Mining News.
claims.verbatim: While Geomorphic AI has not announced whether it has incorporated Earth MRI datasets into its Alaska targeting work,
claims.source_outlet: North of 60 Mining News
claims.notes: Load-bearing framing guard. Consistent with the primary release (C08), which mentions only 'new State airborne geophysical surveys' and names no survey. The deck must present the surveys as public data available to anyone, not as Golden Dyke's inputs.

claims.claim: Geomorphic AI announced a Kazakhstan subsidiary, Geomorphic AI Kazakhstan Ltd., on October 15th.
claims.verbatim: Portland, Oregon and Astana, Kazakhstan--(Newsfile Corp. - October 15, 2026)
claims.source_outlet: Geomorphic AI (company news release via Newsfile)
claims.notes: Subsidiary name verbatim on the page 'Geomorphic AI Kazakhstan Ltd.'. Corroborated by North of 60 Mining News. In window.

claims.claim: Geomorphic AI says it holds more than 650 Kazakh source documents totaling more than 50,000 pages.
claims.verbatim: the Company already holds more than 650 source documents totaling more than 50,000 pages
claims.source_outlet: Geomorphic AI (company news release via Newsfile)
claims.notes: Company claim, attribute as 'Geomorphic says'. Same release says it 'has catalogued more than 5,200 copper, gold, geochemical and geophysical report records spanning 1850 to 2025'. Mining News repeats 650+, 50,000+, 5,200+.

claims.claim: The DGGS Ganes Creek airborne survey covers 8,197 square kilometers, about 3,165 square miles.
claims.verbatim: A total of 25,731 line kilometers were collected, covering 8,197 km2.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys
claims.notes: DGGS gives km2 only; 8,197 km2 / 2.58999 = 3,164.9 sq mi, matching North of 60 Mining News 'covering 3,165 square miles in the Ganes Creek area'. Report GPR 2026-1 dated Jun 2026 (month only; day set to 01).

claims.claim: The Ganes Creek survey collected 25,731 line kilometers of airborne measurements.
claims.verbatim: A total of 25,731 line kilometers were collected, covering 8,197 km2.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys
claims.notes: Matches North of 60 Mining News 'this survey involved 25,731 line-kilometers of airborne geophysical measurements'.

claims.claim: The Ganes Creek survey covers part of the Kuskokwim Mountains west of McGrath.
claims.verbatim: covers part of the Kuskokwim Mountains west of McGrath, Alaska.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys
claims.notes: Mining News says the same. Caution for the map: the metadata bounding box (C21) reaches 154.27 W, which appears to extend east of McGrath's longitude, so draw the block from the DGGS vector data or KMZ (gpr2026_1_ganes_ck-vector_data.zip), not from the rectangle. DGGS also published a separate McGrath survey (C22).

claims.claim: The Ganes Creek survey area includes parts of the Ophir, Medfra, Iditarod and McGrath quadrangles.
claims.verbatim: The survey area includes parts of the Ophir, Medfra, Iditarod, and McGrath quadrangles.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys
claims.notes: Publication page GPR 2026-1 lists the same quadrangles 'Iditarod; McGrath; Medfra; Ophir'. Keywords on that page include the place names 'Ophir', 'Takotna' and 'Flat'.

claims.claim: EON Geosciences Inc. flew the Ganes Creek survey by helicopter from June 21st to September 7th, 2024.
claims.verbatim: EON Geosciences Inc. collected magnetic and radiometric data with a Eurocopter AS350 B2 helicopter,
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys
claims.notes: Dates 'from June 21 to September 7, 2024' on the same page. A second season followed (C18). EON also listed as co-author of GPR 2026-1.

claims.claim: Ganes Creek flying finished with a second helicopter season from June 16th to 25th, 2025.
claims.verbatim: a Eurocopter AS350 B3+ helicopter from June 16 to 25, 2025.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys
claims.notes: Mining News corroborates 'Conducted during 2024 and 2025'.

claims.claim: DGGS published the Ganes Creek magnetic and radiometric survey as Geophysical Report 2026-1 in June.
claims.verbatim: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys Geophysical Report 2026-1, 16 p.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys
claims.notes: Background, outside window. Page shows publication date 'Jun 2026'; title 'Kuskokwim airborne magnetic and radiometric geophysical survey, Ganes Creek, Alaska (2026)'; DOI 10.14509/31746. Mining News 'In June, DGGS published the results'.

claims.claim: The Ganes Creek survey was funded by USGS Earth MRI grants G22AC00475 and G23AC00408.
claims.verbatim: This work was funded by the United States Geological Survey Earth Mapping Resources Initiative (Earth MRI)
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys (GPR 2026-1 metadata)
claims.notes: Grant numbers on the same page as 'grants G22AC00475 and G23AC00408'. Page returned 503 twice before loading on third attempt. Publication page keywords also include 'Earth MRI'.

claims.claim: DGGS metadata bounds the Ganes Creek survey between latitudes 62.21 and 63.36 north and longitudes 154.27 and 158.42 west.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys (GPR 2026-1 metadata)
claims.notes: Bounding coordinates as returned: West -158.421676, East -154.273849, North 63.361469, South 62.210795. For art geometry only; a bounding rectangle is not the survey outline. Prefer the DGGS vector or KMZ files for the actual polygon.

claims.claim: DGGS also published a separate McGrath airborne magnetic and radiometric survey as Geophysical Report 2026-2 in June.
claims.verbatim: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys Geophysical Report 2026-2, 17 p.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys
claims.notes: Same authors and EON Geosciences; page date 'Jun 2026'; keywords include Earth MRI. Not covered by the Mining News article. Its area and line-km were not fetched (gpdata/412 lists the dataset as dated 2024-06-23). Include only to avoid conflating the McGrath and Ganes Creek blocks on a map.

claims.claim: The DGGS Aniak and Little Taylor Mountains survey covers 6,957 square kilometers, about 2,686 square miles.
claims.verbatim: A total of 20,090.5 line kilometers were accepted by DGGS, covering 6,957 km2.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys
claims.notes: 6,957 km2 / 2.58999 = 2,686.1 sq mi, matching Mining News 'covering 2,686 square miles around Aniak and the Little Taylor Mountains in Southwest Alaska'.

claims.claim: DGGS accepted 20,090.5 line kilometers of data from the Aniak and Little Taylor Mountains survey.
claims.verbatim: A total of 20,090.5 line kilometers were accepted by DGGS, covering 6,957 km2.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys
claims.notes: Mining News rounds to 20,090 line-kilometers.

claims.claim: The Aniak and Little Taylor Mountains survey was flown with flight lines 400 meters apart.
claims.verbatim: The survey was flown with a line spacing of 400 meters (m) and a nominal ground clearance of 100 m.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys
claims.notes: Also stated in the GPR 2026-5 metadata. Ganes Creek line spacing was NOT on any fetched page (see killed).

claims.claim: The Aniak and Little Taylor Mountains survey aircraft flew at a nominal 100 meters above the ground.
claims.verbatim: The survey was flown with a line spacing of 400 meters (m) and a nominal ground clearance of 100 m.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys
claims.notes: Nominal, not constant; keep the word nominal.

claims.claim: Terraquest Ltd. flew the Aniak and Little Taylor Mountains survey in a King Air C-90 between June 12th and November 8th, 2025.
claims.verbatim: Terraquest Ltd. collected magnetic and radiometric data with a King Air C-90 from June 12 to November 8, 2025;
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys
claims.notes: Fixed-wing (keyword 'Fixed Wing Survey'), unlike the helicopter-flown Ganes Creek survey. Terraquest also co-author of GPR 2026-5.

claims.claim: Aircraft maintenance paused the Aniak survey from June 28th through September 9th, 2025.
claims.verbatim: aircraft maintenance caused a pause in survey activities from June 28 through September 9, 2025.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys
claims.notes: Minor color detail.

claims.claim: The Aniak and Little Taylor Mountains survey covers parts of the Russian Mission, Sleetmute, Bethel and Taylor Mountains quadrangles of southwestern Alaska.
claims.verbatim: cover parts of the Russian Mission, Sleetmute, Bethel and Taylor Mountains quadrangles of southwestern Alaska
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys
claims.notes: Same wording in the GPR 2026-5 metadata abstract.

claims.claim: DGGS published the Aniak and Little Taylor Mountains survey as Geophysical Report 2026-5 in July.
claims.verbatim: Kuskokwim airborne magnetic and radiometric survey, Aniak and the Little Taylor Mountains, Alaska
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys
claims.notes: Background, outside window. Page shows 'Jul 2026', series 'Geophysical Report 2026-5', 17 p., DOI 10.14509/32087. Mining News 'A second Earth MRI-funded survey released in July'.

claims.claim: The Aniak and Little Taylor Mountains survey was funded by USGS Earth MRI grants G23AC00408 and G24AC00629.
claims.verbatim: United States Geological Survey Earth Mapping Resources Initiative (Earth MRI) grants G23AC00408 and G24AC00629
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys (GPR 2026-5 metadata)
claims.notes: Grant G23AC00408 appears in the funding of BOTH surveys (C20). Publication page keywords include 'Earth MRI;'.

claims.claim: DGGS metadata bounds the Aniak and Little Taylor Mountains survey between latitudes 60.65 and 61.69 north and longitudes 156.69 and 160.10 west.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys (GPR 2026-5 metadata)
claims.notes: As returned: West -160.098112, East -156.694820, North 61.693172, South 60.651119. For art geometry only; use the DGGS vector or KMZ files (gpr2026_005-aniak-ltl-taylor-vector_data.zip) for the outline. The two survey boxes do not overlap (Ganes Creek south bound 62.21 N is north of Aniak north bound 61.69 N).

claims.claim: DGGS tags the Aniak survey with the Kuskokwim River, the Little Taylor Mountains and the village of Chuathbaluk among its keywords.
claims.verbatim: Kolmakof River; Kuskokwim River; Little Taylor Mountains;
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys
claims.notes: Chuathbaluk appears in the segment 'Bristol Bay Region Mining District; Buckstock River; Chichitnok River; Chicken Creek; Chikululnuk Creek; Chuathbaluk;'. Keywords also include 'Aniak', 'Aniak River', 'Holitna River', 'Crow Village', 'Napaimiut', 'Taylor Mountains Mine'. Keywords are tags, not a statement that a place lies inside the block; for the map, word it as places named in the survey record.

claims.claim: Both surveys collected magnetic data with cesium-vapour sensors and radiometric data with two gamma-ray spectrometers each.
claims.verbatim: Radiometric data were collected with two Radiation Solutions RS-500 series multi-channel gamma-ray spectrometers.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys
claims.notes: Ganes Creek page 'Magnetic data were collected with a Scintrex CS-3 cesium-vapour split-beam sensor.' Aniak page (gpdata/414) 'Magnetic data were collected with a Geometrics Inc G-822A cesium-vapour magnetometer;' and 'radiometric data were collected with two (2) Radiation Solutions RS-500 series multi-channel gamma-ray spectrometers'. One spectrometer looks down, the other up to detect atmospheric radon.

claims.claim: DGGS says the Ganes Creek survey will improve understanding of the geology and mineral potential of the central Kuskokwim River region.
claims.verbatim: will improve the understanding of the geology and mineral potential of the central Kuskokwim River region,
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys
claims.notes: Page also says the survey is meant to encourage resource exploration. No equivalent purpose sentence on the Aniak gpdata page.

claims.claim: The two surveys together add more than 45,800 line kilometers of new geophysical data, according to North of 60 Mining News.
claims.verbatim: These surveys alone represent more than 45,800 line-kilometers of new geophysical information
claims.source_outlet: North of 60 Mining News
claims.notes: Arithmetic check against primary DGGS figures: 25,731 + 20,090.5 = 45,821.5 line-km. Consistent.

claims.claim: The two surveys together cover approximately 5,850 square miles of Southwest Alaska, according to North of 60 Mining News.
claims.verbatim: covering approximately 5,850 square miles of Southwest Alaska.
claims.source_outlet: North of 60 Mining News
claims.notes: Arithmetic check: 8,197 + 6,957 = 15,154 km2 = 5,851 sq mi. Consistent. About 15,150 square kilometers if metric is wanted.

claims.claim: The USGS Earth Mapping Resources Initiative was launched in 2019.
claims.verbatim: Earth MRI was launched in 2019.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Geological Survey
claims.notes: Background. Undated program page; date_of_source is the fetch date. Mining News agrees 'Launched in 2019'. USGS landing page says 'Earth MRI began in 2019.'

claims.claim: Earth MRI is an initiative within the USGS Mineral Resources Program that maps geology to help find new critical mineral resources.
claims.verbatim: find new critical and other mineral resources,
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Geological Survey
claims.notes: Background. Same page 'Earth MRI is an initiative within the USGS Mineral Resources Program.' and 'Earth MRI is modernizing mapping of the Nation's surface and subsurface.'

claims.claim: USGS says the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act invested in Earth MRI.
claims.verbatim: the Infrastructure, Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) invested in Earth MRI.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Geological Survey
claims.notes: Background. No dollar total on the page. The USGS Alaska Science Center page lists a headline 'USGS invests $3.6 million in Bipartisan Infrastructure Law funding to map critical minerals across Alaska' (2024), not tied to these two surveys; do not connect that figure to Ganes Creek or Aniak.

claims.claim: USGS says Earth MRI partners with state geological surveys, federal agencies, private industry, tribes and universities.
claims.verbatim: We partner with State geological surveys, Federal agencies, private industry, Tribes, universities and others.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Geological Survey
claims.notes: Background. The DGGS link to Earth MRI for these surveys is proven by the grant numbers in C20 and C31.

claims.claim: USGS calls Alaska a priority focus region for critical minerals with significant known or suspected potential.
claims.verbatim: Alaska has significant known or suspected critical mineral potential and is a priority focus region
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Geological Survey Alaska Science Center
claims.notes: Background. Undated program page; date is fetch date.

claims.claim: The FAA proposed its rule for routine drone flights beyond visual line of sight on August 7th, 2025.
claims.verbatim: Normalizing Unmanned Aircraft Systems Beyond Visual Line of Sight Operations
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register (Office of the Federal Register)
claims.notes: Background. Type 'Proposed Rule', document 2025-14992, publication_date 2025-08-07, comments closed 2025-10-06. RUNNER-UP story. The HTML page redirected to unblock.federalregister.gov; the API JSON is the same official record.

claims.claim: The proposed beyond visual line of sight rule carries RIN 2120-AL82 and would add a new Part 108 to Title 14.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register (Office of the Federal Register)
claims.notes: cfr_references list Title 14 Parts 36, 43, 45, 48, 89, 91, 107, 108, 119, 133, 135, 137 and 146. 'Part 108' does not appear in the abstract itself; safer phrasing is 'the rule that touches 14 CFR Part 108, widely called Part 108'. Second RIN 1652-AA80 is TSA's.

claims.claim: The proposed rule says the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 directs its development.
claims.verbatim: The FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 directs the development of this proposed rule.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register (Office of the Federal Register)
claims.notes: Background.

claims.claim: As of October 22nd the Federal Register showed no final rule for normalizing drone flights beyond visual line of sight, only the 2025 proposal and two 2026 comment reopenings.
claims.verbatim: Normalizing Unmanned Aircraft Systems Beyond Visual Line of Sight Operations; Reopening of Comment Period; Denial of Extension
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register (Office of the Federal Register)
claims.notes: In window (checked October 22nd, the day after run date). Query returned 11 documents; every 'Normalizing Unmanned Aircraft Systems' item is type Proposed Rule (2025-08-07, 2025-09-29, 2026-01-28, 2026-02-10). The scout's BVLOS term query (11 results since 2026-01-01) likewise had no such final rule. The 2026 Unified Agenda (2026-08-14) lists the action at 'Final Rule Stage', a projection. Phrase as 'had not been published in the Federal Register as of October 22nd'.

claims.claim: Executive Order 14307, signed June 6th, 2025, ordered a final beyond visual line of sight rule within 240 days.
claims.verbatim: A final rule shall be published within 240 days of the date of this order, as appropriate.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register (Executive Order 14307, Unleashing American Drone Dominance)
claims.notes: Background. Section 4(a) directs the Secretary of Transportation, through the FAA, to propose a rule enabling routine BVLOS operations within 30 days and closes with the verbatim sentence. Signature line 'THE WHITE HOUSE, June 6, 2025.' The order includes 'as appropriate'; avoid 'required by law'.

claims.claim: The executive order's 240 day target for a final drone rule fell on February 1st, 2026.
claims.verbatim: Executive Order 14307 set a 240-day deadline for the final rule that expired February 1, 2026.
claims.source_outlet: PickDrones
claims.notes: Independently verified by arithmetic from the primary order (C47): June 6th, 2025 plus 240 days is February 1st, 2026. Background. Call it a target, since the order says 'as appropriate'.

claims.claim: UAF's drone program completed a 1,000 kilometer test flight carrying human blood samples for the International Testing Agency.
claims.verbatim: successfully completed a 1,000-kilometer test flight carrying human blood samples
claims.source_outlet: UAF Geophysical Institute
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, outside window (September 17th, Rod Boyce). Sentence continues 'for the International Testing Agency, which investigates doping by athletes'. Corroborated by Cargo Newswire (2026-09-29). The GI release does not call it a 'round trip' or say 'autonomous'; Cargo Newswire uses 'autonomous heavy-lift aircraft'.

claims.claim: The test flight began and ended at Nenana Municipal Airport on August 19th.
claims.verbatim: The test began and ended at Nenana Municipal Airport on Aug. 19.
claims.source_outlet: UAF Geophysical Institute
claims.notes: Background. Cargo Newswire 'The test flight took place on August 19, 2026.' No route beyond start and end is published.

claims.claim: The ACUASI flight lasted 8 hours and 47 minutes.
claims.verbatim: The 8-hour, 47-minute flight by the Alaska Center for Unmanned Aircraft Systems Integration
claims.source_outlet: UAF Geophysical Institute
claims.notes: Background. Cargo Newswire corroborates 8 hours and 47 minutes.

claims.claim: The Windracers ULTRA used in the test has a 200 pound cargo capacity.
claims.verbatim: a 200-pound cargo capacity
claims.source_outlet: UAF Geophysical Institute
claims.notes: Background. Same page 'Windracers, which builds the ULTRA aircraft used in the test flight.'

claims.claim: The ULTRA has a 31 foot wingspan.
claims.verbatim: a 31-foot wingspan
claims.source_outlet: UAF Geophysical Institute
claims.notes: Background.

claims.claim: The ULTRA has a range of about 600 miles.
claims.verbatim: a range of about 600 miles
claims.source_outlet: UAF Geophysical Institute
claims.notes: Background. Sanity check: 1,000 km is about 621 miles, slightly over the 'about 600 miles' figure; both are approximate, so do not juxtapose them as if the flight exceeded rated range.

claims.claim: ACUASI owns two of the twin engine ULTRA aircraft.
claims.verbatim: ACUASI owns two of the twin-engine aircraft
claims.source_outlet: UAF Geophysical Institute
claims.notes: Background.

claims.claim: The International Testing Agency's 2022 Doha trials used quadcopters over distances of up to 20 kilometers.
claims.verbatim: over distances of up to 20 kilometers.
claims.source_outlet: UAF Geophysical Institute
claims.notes: Background. Fetched text attributes quadcopters and Doha 2022 in the surrounding sentence; only the distance phrase was returned verbatim.

claims.claim: ACUASI Director Cathy Cahill said "If it's an emergency, you don't want to trust it to an amateur."
claims.verbatim: If it's an emergency, you don't want to trust it to an amateur.
claims.source_outlet: UAF Geophysical Institute
claims.notes: Background. Title on page 'ACUASI Director'. Also verbatim 'The competency of ACUASI pilots is truly outstanding,'.

claims.claim: UAF says it runs one of nine FAA-designated unmanned aircraft systems test sites.
claims.verbatim: one of nine FAA-designated unmanned aircraft systems test sites.
claims.source_outlet: UAF Geophysical Institute
claims.notes: Background, UAF self-description.

claims.claim: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced roughly $249 million in federal funding for the Alaska Railroad to finish the stalled Port MacKenzie rail link.
claims.verbatim: The Alaska Railroad will receive $249 million in federal funding to finish work on the stalled 32-mile rail link.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Mat-Su Sentinel, Tim Bradner)
claims.notes: THIRD story. Announced Monday October 19th. KTUU/Alaska's News Source (2026-10-21) also reports $249 million; ADN (Iris Samuels, 2026-10-21) writes '$250 million'. Use 'about $250 million' or attribute the exact figure. No primary DOT release fetched. No AI tie in any source.

claims.claim: The Port MacKenzie rail link the grant would finish is 32 miles long.
claims.verbatim: the stalled 32-mile rail link connecting the Matanuska-Susitna Borough's Port MacKenzie
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Mat-Su Sentinel, Tim Bradner)
claims.notes: Corroborated by KTUU/Alaska's News Source ('32-mile rail line').

claims.claim: The Department of Energy opened about $38 million in grants for electric reliability and affordability in Alaska, according to Alaska's News Source.
claims.verbatim: $38 million in grants to shore up electric reliability and affordability in Alaska
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU), Wil Courtney
claims.notes: Page stamp 'Published: Oct. 21, 2026 at 5:10 PM AKDT' though URL path reads 2026/10/22. ADN gives 'more than $30 million' for electric grid resilience projects, consistent but less precise. No funds awarded yet. Program name not given; no primary DOE notice fetched.

claims.claim: The federal funding announcements for Alaska arrived as the midterm elections approached, according to the Anchorage Daily News.
claims.verbatim: as the midterm elections have approached
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (Iris Samuels)
claims.notes: Political framing; attribute to ADN. KTUU's headline independently says 'amid wave election-season federal funding'. ADN also reports Sen. Sullivan denies the grants are a political move; include that if the framing is used.

claims.claim: The DGGS McGrath airborne survey acquired 86,319 line kilometers of magnetic and radiometric data.
claims.verbatim: A total of 86,319 line - kilometers were acquired.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys, Geophysical Report 2026-2
claims.notes: Added by the showrunner from the report PDF text extracted with scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py on 2026-10-22 (copy in out/2026-10-21/data). Publication month from the DGGS new reports listing; survey facts are background to the October 20th announcement.

claims.claim: EON Geosciences flew the McGrath survey with four fixed wing aircraft from June 23rd to September 5th, 2024, and from June 14th to July 26th, 2025.
claims.verbatim: collected magnetic and radiometric data with four fixed wing aircraft from June 23 to September 5, 2024, then from June 14 to July 26, 2025.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys, Geophysical Report 2026-2
claims.notes: Added by the showrunner from the report PDF text extracted with scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py on 2026-10-22 (copy in out/2026-10-21/data). Publication month from the DGGS new reports listing; survey facts are background to the October 20th announcement.

claims.claim: The McGrath survey was flown with lines 400 meters apart at a nominal 100 meters above the ground.
claims.verbatim: The McGrath survey was flown with a line spacing of 400 meters (m) and a nominal ground clearance of 100 m.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys, Geophysical Report 2026-2
claims.notes: Added by the showrunner from the report PDF text extracted with scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py on 2026-10-22 (copy in out/2026-10-21/data). Publication month from the DGGS new reports listing; survey facts are background to the October 20th announcement.
